Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple ill-defined nodular opacities, most prominent in the right mid and left upper lung zones, with a visible tubular structure suggesting a feeding artery consistent with pulmonary arteriovenous malformations (PAVMs). Given the risk of paradoxical embolism and hemorrhage associated with PAVMs, coil embolization is the standard first-line management for suitable lesions.
